name: Toyota MR2 Spyder
reliability: 8/10 — the ZZW30 is the lightest, simplest MR2 and, kept in tune, a dependable little roadster whose low weight flatters its modest power. Two things define ownership. First, the pre-2003 1ZZ-FE is a known oil-burner: the original piston-ring design can consume oil, so you check the level religiously and value a car with the updated rings. Second, the early SMT automated-manual is the weak point — jerky and expensive to fix — so the plain 5-speed manual is the one to buy. Do those two things and it is cheap, tossable fun.
cost_to_own: Insurance: Moderate (small two-seat convertible) · Maintenance ~$450/yr · Excellent fuel economy for a sports car · Values are firming as the last, cheapest mid-engine Toyota — clean manuals lead
popular_mods: A hardtop and a wind deflector — the biggest comfort and refinement upgrade for the open car
Quality coilovers and a sway-bar set — the light chassis sharpens up beautifully
Sticky 200-treadwear tires — grip transforms a 2,200 lb car more than horsepower would
A modest intake/header/exhaust for a little more sound and response (big power means an engine swap)
Honest take: this car is about lightness and balance, not power — spend on suspension, tires, and a manual, not a turbo
oil_interval: Every 5,000 miles — and check the level often on pre-2003 cars

generations.2000–2002: The launch Spyder — 138 hp 1ZZ-FE, 5-speed manual, and a featherweight ~2,200 lb curb weight. Pure, simple mid-engine convertible fun. Early 1ZZ engines are the most prone to oil consumption.
generations.2003–2005: Late US cars got the updated pistons/rings that largely cured the oil burning, minor styling and interior tweaks, and remain the ones to seek out. A 6-speed SMT was optional from 2002 but the manual is preferred.

common_issues: Pre-2003 1ZZ-FE oil consumption — check the oil level often; updated rings on later cars fixed most cases
The SMT sequential automated-manual is jerky and costly to repair — favor the conventional 5-speed
Convertible-top wear and rear-window clouding with age and sun
Pre-cat material can break down and be ingested on high-mile 1ZZ engines — a known Toyota-four concern
Very small cabin and no cargo space to speak of — a weekend toy, not a daily hauler
maintenance_tips: Check the oil level every couple of fill-ups on any pre-2003 car and top up promptly
Buy the 5-speed manual; budget for specialist repair if you take on an SMT car
Keep the convertible top clean and treated, and store it out of the sun when possible
Address the pre-cat concern proactively on high-mile engines to protect the cylinders
Otherwise it is basic, cheap upkeep — this is one of the most affordable mid-engine cars to own
